**2. Establishment of Terms of Reference**
The draft Terms of Reference were circulated prior to the meeting. Members reviewed the document and discussed the scope of the Committee’s authority. It was agreed that the Committee would have oversight of capital works, maintenance schedules, compliance audits, and major procurement decisions affecting the cold chain.

**Moved by:** Robert Callahan
**Seconded by:** Priya Nair
**Carried unanimously.**

**3. Review of Existing Cold Storage Assets**
Robert Callahan presented a summary of the current asset base, including the main warehouse at Truganina, the regional hub in Launceston, and two transport depots in Brisbane and Perth. He noted that the average age of the evaporator units across the network was 11 years, and that energy consumption had increased by approximately 8% year-on-year. A full condition assessment was scheduled for the next quarter.

**4. Compliance Update**
David Osei reported that the most recent internal audit of temperature logging had identified three instances of data gaps during the previous month, all related to a faulty sensor in Freezer Bay 3. The sensor had been replaced, and corrective action was underway. He recommended that the Committee consider a policy for mandatory backup sensors in all high-risk bays.

**5. Financial Report**
Fiona MacAllister presented the preliminary budget position for the 2018–19 financial year. The cold chain capital expenditure envelope was set at $2.4 million, with the largest single item being the replacement of the dock levellers at the Truganina site. She noted that the actual spend to date was in line with the forecast.

**6. Procurement Update**
Grace Liu advised that the tender for the supply of refrigerated transport units had closed on 23 February 2018. Three responses were received, and a shortlist of two suppliers (ColdHaul Logistics and TransFridge Solutions) had been prepared for interview. The evaluation panel would report back to the Committee at the next meeting.

**7. General Business**
- Priya Nair raised a concern regarding the availability of spare parts for the older refrigeration units. It was agreed that a stocktake of critical spares would be completed by the end of March.
- Dr. Voss confirmed that the Committee’s minutes would be published on the internal governance portal within five working days of each meeting.

**5. Operational Update – July 2018** (continued)

The Committee noted that the temperature monitoring system upgrade at the Altona North facility is scheduled to commence in October 2018. **5. Operational Update – July 2018** (continued)

Priya Nair reported that the Preston Distribution Centre operated at 96.4% capacity utilisation for the month, with a total of 1,847 pallet movements recorded. The cold storage facility at the Dandenong South site handled 2,310 pallets, maintaining an average temperature of −21.3°C across the freezer chambers, which remains within the approved operating band of −18°C to −25°C.

Ms. Nair noted that the chiller section at the Altona North facility experienced a minor temperature fluctuation on 24 July, with readings peaking at 4.8°C for a period of approximately 40 minutes. The issue was traced to a faulty door seal on Bay 7, which was replaced the same day. The incident was logged in the temperature monitoring system as event reference TMS-2018-0714, and no product was affected.

The Committee reviewed the maintenance schedule for the upcoming month. The scheduled defrost cycle for the freezer units at the Sunshine West site is planned for 12–14 August, and the facility will operate on reduced capacity during this period. Ms. Nair confirmed that customers had been notified of the planned downtime and that deliveries had been rescheduled accordingly.

**6. Facility and Equipment Report**

Mr. David Tran, Facilities Manager, provided an update on the condition of the refrigeration plant at the Dandenong South site. The annual compressor service is scheduled for 3–5 September, and the service contract with CoolTech Refrigeration Services covers the required parts and labour. Mr. Tran noted that the contractor had been advised of the access requirements and that a site induction would be arranged for the service team.

Mr. Tran also reported that the replacement of the evaporator fan motors at the Preston Distribution Centre had been completed on 18 July, one week ahead of the planned completion date. The work was carried out by the in-house maintenance team, and the motors have been tested and are operating within specification.

The Committee noted that the temperature monitoring system upgrade at the Altona North facility is scheduled to commence in October 2018. The upgrade will involve the installation of new sensors and the replacement of the existing data logger software. Mr. Tran advised that the system would be installed in stages to minimise disruption to operations, and that the facility would continue to operate normally during the installation period.

**7. Logistics and Transport Update**

Mr. James O'Connor, Logistics Manager, reported on transport operations for July. The on-time delivery rate was 97.2%, which is slightly below the target of 98%. The shortfall was attributed to two delivery delays caused by unexpected traffic conditions on the Hume Highway, and one delay resulting from a vehicle breakdown near Geelong. The breakdown was resolved within four hours, and the affected deliveries were completed the same day.

Mr. O'Connor noted that the trial of the new refrigerated trailer fleet had been completed successfully. The two trial trailers, which were operated for a period of six weeks, recorded an average temperature variance of ±0.8°C, which is within the acceptable range of ±1.5°C. The Committee discussed the trial results and agreed that the performance of the trailers was satisfactory.

The Committee also noted that the fuel surcharge applied to customer invoices had been adjusted in line with the current diesel price index. The surcharge rate for August is set at 3.2%, which reflects the average fuel price for the previous month.

Ms. Chen reported that there were no lost-time injuries recorded at any of the company's facilities during July. The total recordable injury rate for the 2018/19 financial year to date remains at 2.1 cases per million hours worked, which is below the industry benchmark.
